channel.title: The Indicator from Planet Money
channel.description:
A bite-sized show about big ideas. From the people who make Planet Money, The Indicator helps you make sense of what's happening in today's economy. It's a quick hit of insight into money, work, and business. Monday through Friday, in 10 minutes or less.
Sign up for our newsletter.

item.description:

item.title: Why the 'good old days' of American manufacturing are long gone
item.description:
Harvard professor Willy Shih tells us why the manufacturing renaissance President Trump envisioned has not come to pass and how a different type of resurgence may still be possible. 

Willy Shih’s book is Where Does My Stuff Come From?: The Powerful Economics Behind Global Supply Chains.

Fact checking by Sierra Juarez.

item.title: How a tribal water deal could put a price tag on the Colorado River
item.description:
What’s stopping a pipeline that would bring running water from the Colorado River to tribal lands who’ve long gone without it? Today on the show, the multi-billion dollar project to bring clean water to three tribes in the Four Corners, and the complicated economics behind why some states are trying to slow it down. 

This story was reported in collaboration with Mark Olalde from ProPublica. Fact checking by Sierra Juarez.

item.title: Three influencer types and how they generate money
item.description:
Influencers are a pervasive aspect of the creator economy and one of the most desired career paths for young Americans today. But how are these creators making their money? Today, we talk to Stanford researcher, Angèle Christin, about three common archetypes that explain why influencers behave the way they do. 

Her new book about it is called “Gurus, Hucksters, Entertainers How Influencers Reshaped Social Media.”

Fact checking by Sierra Juarez.
